neutral_facts.value: The accused, a woman and her husband, were involved in a scheme where the husband, who was a Head Constable in the Punjab Police, extracted money from an informant by making false promises of arranging a job in the Police. The deal was for Rs.1,40,000/-, with Rs.70,000/- paid in advance. The informant paid the amount to the husband, who handed it over to his wife, the accused. The husband and wife then went to collect the remaining Rs.20,000/- from the informant's house. No employment was provided, and the money was not refunded. The husband was found guilty of cheating, and the wife was also convicted for the same offence. The prosecution case and evidence indicated that the husband played the primary role in the commission of the offence, while the wife had a subsidiary role.
